text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Parliament failed on Thursday to finish a debate the draft law on compulsory military service.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele has come forward with a plan to reduce the number of ministers to 16 from 25.
- The Ministry of Economics says that compensation must be paid to former land owners who recieved compensation vouchers instaed of their property.

- The Latvian state-owned Railroad company and the Bank of New York have signed a credit agreement under which Latvian railways will receive a loan of $6.5 million to modernize its telecomunication system. This is the first loan provided by an American bank without a Latvian government guarantee.
- Latvia has been elected a member of the UN Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC).
- Latvia established diplomatic relations with Gabon.
- Russia's Aeroflot suspended its flights to Riga after Latvian aviation authorities refused to confirm its winter schedule. The two countries' transport ministries are locked in a row over parity.
- The telecommunication tariff council has approved new tariffs for Lattelekom's digital line service.
